items.title: How Coinbase used Code Connect to guide agents and shrink token costs
items.excerpt: Coinbase's design systems team measured what Code Connect actually does for coding agents: 22.5% lower token cost and better design-to-code adherence, because agents stop hallucinating component and asset names.
items.why: First hard number on what a design system mapping buys you in agent workflows — the design system becomes a cost lever, not just a consistency lever.

items.title: Solidworks users spend “blue tokens” on AI drawings, insights and more
items.excerpt: Dassault Systèmes introduced a consumption-based "blue token" currency for AI usage across the 3DExperience platform, with each license carrying a free allocation and 25,000-token packs sold on top.
items.why: AI features inside a core design tool stop being free — metered credits change how product teams budget and ration AI in daily CAD work.

items.title: SunCubes uses AI simulation to develop UAV charging systems
items.excerpt: SunCubes ran thermal, structural and aerodynamic analysis of its wireless energy-transfer hardware through AI-assisted SimScale simulation instead of iterating on physical prototypes.
items.why: A concrete hardware-design case where simulation-first replaces build-and-test — the physical AI loop applied to real product development.

items.title: Siemens Realize Live 2026
items.excerpt: A report from Siemens' Realize Live on how Xcelerator is shaping up as the company pushes AI and agents deeper into the industrial design and engineering stack.
items.why: Shows where the big PLM vendors are placing AI in the product-design pipeline — relevant to anyone whose design work ends up in an engineering handoff.

items.title: I Let AI Design Tools Build My Portfolio Site — Clients Noticed
items.excerpt: A designer hands the first version of a portfolio site to AI design tools and reports what the generated layout got right, what needed rebuilding, and how clients reacted to the result.
items.why: A first-person account of where prompt-generated layouts hold up and where a designer still has to take the wheel.

items.title: Designing an AI YouTube Thumbnail Workflow That Keeps Its Context
items.excerpt: Behind an upload button and one prompt field sits a chain of contracts — image accepted, concept interpreted, style selected, candidates generated — and the piece maps how to keep context intact across each step.
items.why: Treats a generative feature as a sequence of product decisions rather than one prompt box — a reusable pattern for designing any AI creative tool.

items.title: I Redesigned My Blog With Claude Design and Claude Code in Less Than a Day
items.excerpt: A walkthrough of taking Anthropic's new Claude Design from concept to shipped site, handing the visual direction to Claude Design and the implementation to Claude Code in a single day.
items.why: Early hands-on with Claude Design as a real design surface, showing where the design tool ends and the coding agent begins.

items.title: Adobe releases Photoshop 27.10
items.excerpt: Photoshop 27.10 brings prompt-based image editing into the standard editor and adds a full AI Assisted Editor mode, with masks and visual markup used to keep prompts precise.
items.why: Prompting moves inside the layer stack of the industry's default raster tool — the edit stays targeted instead of regenerating whole frames.

items.title: NVIDIA Finally Announces Launch Date For Its Controversial DLSS 5
items.excerpt: NVIDIA set a launch date for DLSS 5, the neural rendering update that artists have argued either preserves or destroys their original intent on screen.
items.why: Generative upscaling now sits between the artist's frame and the viewer's screen — a real-time craft question for anyone shipping 3D visuals.

items.title: Is Nvidia's DLSS 5 an AI slop machine or a game-changing technology?
items.excerpt: Creative Bloq weighs the artist backlash against DLSS 5's neural frame generation against the claim that it gets rendered output closer to what artists originally intended.
items.why: The clearest statement yet of the craft argument over generated pixels in the final render — authorship versus fidelity.

items.title: Create Procedural UE5 Animations Based on Music with This Tool
items.excerpt: A new tool drives procedural Unreal Engine 5 animation directly from an audio track, turning music structure into motion without hand-keying every beat.
items.why: Signal-driven motion instead of manual keyframes — a procedural shortcut motion designers can lift straight into production.

items.title: Making kyōwa possible with AI
items.excerpt: On unbundling the Send button so that words can work as sketches — a rethink of the chat interface where text becomes a malleable design material rather than a committed message.
items.why: Attacks the most copied AI interaction pattern — the prompt-and-send box — and proposes a genuinely different interface model.

items.title: Color scheming with Perplexity tetrads
items.excerpt: A case study in using generative AI to build accessible color palettes, working tetrad color relationships through Perplexity and checking them against contrast requirements.
items.why: A repeatable AI method for a foundational token decision — palette generation with accessibility checked, not assumed.

items.title: The call for an agentic standard: We need to stop shipping the same form four different times
items.excerpt: One description, four renderers: every assistant draws its own version of your UI, and the maintenance bill lands on the team that already owns the button component. MCP settled the plumbing; the rendering layer hasn't.
items.why: Names the next standards fight after MCP — who owns the rendered interface when four assistants each redraw your design system.

items.title: Graphic designers are trying to fix people's terrible AI flyers
items.excerpt: A viral Instagram trend has professional designers redoing strangers' AI-generated flyers, turning the gap between generated output and finished design work into public demonstration.
items.why: A visible, popular argument about what generated output still misses — and designers making the value of craft legible to non-designers.

items.title: Engineering AI into the product development lifecycle
items.excerpt: Google Cloud's DORA research across nearly 5,000 technology professionals found 90% now use AI at work for a median of two hours a day — roughly a quarter of the working day — and the piece argues teams are wiring it in at the wrong end of the lifecycle.
items.why: Data on where AI actually lands in product teams' day, and the case for moving it upstream into definition rather than the final build step.

items.title: Software engineers' new job isn't writing code — it's designing the boundaries AI agents can't break
items.excerpt: With agents handling routine generation, the work shifts to designing guardrails — semantic contracts and feedback loops that define what the system may and may not do.
items.why: The same role shift is arriving for designers: authoring the constraints an agent works inside instead of the artifact itself.

items.title: Google says its new Gemini 3.8 Flash model 'works harder' but might cost more
items.excerpt: Gemini 3.8 Flash arrives weeks after its predecessor, adding more reasoning steps and iterative tool calls on complex tasks at the same introductory price of $0.75 per million input tokens.
items.why: The fast, cheap tier that powers most design-tool integrations gets more agentic — with a cost profile teams have to watch.

items.title: The case against intuitive design in enterprise software
items.excerpt: An argument that chasing consumer-grade intuitiveness in enterprise tools makes expert workflows slower, and that density and learnability often beat immediate legibility.
items.why: Directly relevant as AI assistants get bolted onto enterprise UIs — a reminder that expert software has different design targets.

items.title: Honor Robot Phone hands-on: A gimbal phone experiment with promising results
items.excerpt: Honor crammed a motorized gimbal camera into a phone body, a hardware experiment that puts a moving, semi-autonomous element into a device people hold.
items.why: Physical AI arriving in consumer product design — an industrial-design problem of housing motion inside a familiar object.

items.title: How to match images to your brand's aesthetic with Adobe Stock AI Studio
items.excerpt: Adobe walks through Adobe Stock AI Studio, generating and adapting stock imagery so that results stay inside a brand's existing visual language rather than defaulting to generic AI style.
items.why: Brand consistency is the hardest part of generated imagery; this shows the vendor's answer to steering output toward an established aesthetic.

items.title: 9 Designs That Inspired Meshtimes, One of Tech's Most Creative Minds | Source Material
items.excerpt: Figma's Source Material series walks through nine designs that shaped Meshtimes' creative point of view, tracing where a distinctive visual sensibility actually comes from.
items.why: A counterweight to generated defaults — where personal visual reference libraries come from and why they still differentiate work.
